title: Circuits with a closed-form solution: dividers, an RC filter and series RLC circuits

cases.title: Voltage divider of 1 kohm and 3 kohm on 10 V
cases.tolerance_note: chosen here: a linear solve of a three-node circuit, so only rounding is accepted
cases.source: J. W. Nilsson and S. A. Riedel, Electric Circuits, the voltage-divider circuit: Vout = Vin R2/(R1 + R2)

cases.title: Loaded divider: 1 kohm over two 1 kohm resistors in parallel on 10 V
cases.tolerance_note: chosen here: the parallel pair is 500 ohm, so Vout = 10 x 500/1500 exactly up to rounding
cases.source: J. W. Nilsson and S. A. Riedel, Electric Circuits, resistors in parallel and the voltage-divider circuit

cases.title: First-order RC low-pass: gain at the corner frequency
cases.tolerance_note: chosen here: C = 1/(2 pi R f) for f = 1 kHz, so |H| = 1/sqrt(2) up to the rounding of C
cases.source: J. W. Nilsson and S. A. Riedel, Electric Circuits, frequency response of the first-order low-pass filter: |H(j w_c)| = 1/sqrt(2) at w_c = 1/(R C)

cases.title: First-order RC low-pass: phase at the corner frequency
cases.tolerance_note: chosen here: the phase is -arctan(w R C) = -45 degrees up to the rounding of C
cases.source: J. W. Nilsson and S. A. Riedel, Electric Circuits, frequency response of the first-order low-pass filter: phase = -arctan(w/w_c)

cases.title: Series RLC (10 ohm, 1 mH, 1 uF): gain across the resistor at resonance
cases.tolerance_note: chosen here: at f0 = 1/(2 pi sqrt(LC)) the reactances cancel, so the resistor takes the whole source voltage
cases.source: J. W. Nilsson and S. A. Riedel, Electric Circuits, the series RLC band-pass: at the resonant frequency w0 = 1/sqrt(LC) the output across R equals the input

cases.title: Series RLC (10 ohm, 1 mH, 1 uF): gain across the capacitor at resonance equals Q
cases.tolerance_note: chosen here: at resonance the capacitor voltage is Q = sqrt(L/C)/R times the source, exactly up to rounding of the frequency
cases.source: J. W. Nilsson and S. A. Riedel, Electric Circuits, the series RLC circuit: at w0 the voltage across the capacitor is Q times the source with Q = (1/R) sqrt(L/C)

cases.title: RC step response after one time constant
cases.tolerance_note: chosen here: wider than the error of the trapezoidal rule at 100 steps per time constant plus the first backward Euler step and the 1 ns rise of the source
cases.source: J. W. Nilsson and S. A. Riedel, Electric Circuits, the step response of an RC circuit: v(t) = V (1 - exp(-t/(R C))), which is 1 - 1/e = 0.6321 at t = R C

cases.title: Underdamped series RLC step response at 100 us
cases.tolerance_note: chosen here: wider than the error of the trapezoidal rule at 1000 steps over three quarters of a ring period, the first backward Euler step and the 1 ns rise of the source
cases.source: J. W. Nilsson and S. A. Riedel, Electric Circuits, the step response of a series RLC circuit, underdamped: v(t) = V (1 - exp(-a t) (cos(wd t) + (a/wd) sin(wd t))) with a = R/(2L) = 5000 1/s and wd = sqrt(1/(L C) - a^2) = 31224.99 rad/s

cases.title: Diode with a 1 kohm series resistor on 5 V (IS 1e-14 A, n 1): voltage across the diode
cases.tolerance_note: chosen here: Newton-Raphson stops when the change is below reltol*|v| + vntol twice in a row, which leaves an error of about 1e-5 V on the junction voltage, so 1e-4 V is wider than needed and still far below the 26 mV scale of the junction
cases.source: Shockley ideal diode equation I = Is (exp(Vd/(n Vt)) - 1) with Vt = k T / q (k = 1.380649e-23 J/K, q = 1.602176634e-19 C, T = 300.15 K, the temperature of config/sim.cfg), A. S. Sedra and K. C. Smith, Microelectronic Circuits, the diode forward characteristic; the series circuit Vs = I R + Vd has the closed form I = (n Vt / R) W((Is R / (n Vt)) exp((Vs + Is R) / (n Vt))) - Is with W the principal branch of the Lambert W function (R. M. Corless, G. H. Gonnet, D. E. G. Hare, D. J. Jeffrey and D. E. Knuth, On the Lambert W function, Advances in Computational Mathematics 5, 1996); W was evaluated by Newton iteration on ln w + w = ln x and checked against a bisection of the same equation

cases.title: Half-wave rectifier at the peak of a 5 V, 1 kHz sine (diode IS 1e-14 A, n 1, load 2.2 kohm): load voltage
cases.tolerance_note: chosen here: Newton-Raphson stops when the change is below reltol*|v| + vntol twice in a row, which leaves an error of about 1e-5 V on the junction voltage, so 1e-4 V is wider than needed and still far below the 26 mV scale of the junction; the circuit has no reactive element, so every time step is the static circuit at the source voltage of that instant
cases.source: Shockley ideal diode equation I = Is (exp(Vd/(n Vt)) - 1) with Vt = k T / q (k = 1.380649e-23 J/K, q = 1.602176634e-19 C, T = 300.15 K, the temperature of config/sim.cfg), A. S. cases.title: Half-wave rectifier in the negative half cycle (t = 0.75 ms): the diode blocks and the load voltage is zero
cases.tolerance_note: chosen here: the reverse current is IS plus the conductance gmin (1e-12 S) times 5 V, about 5e-12 A, which is 1.1e-8 V across 2.2 kohm
cases.source: A. S. Sedra and K. C. Smith, Microelectronic Circuits, the half-wave rectifier: the diode does not conduct while the source is negative, so the load carries no current

cases.title: NMOS inverter with a 1 kohm load, input 0.5 V (below the threshold of 1 V): the transistor is cut off

netlist: nmos inverter with a resistive load

cases.tolerance_note: chosen here: the square-law equations are solved by Newton-Raphson, which stops with an error of about 1e-5 V on a 4 V node, so 1e-4 V is wider than needed
cases.source: H. Shichman and D. A. Hodges, Modeling and simulation of insulated-gate field-effect transistor switching circuits, IEEE Journal of Solid-State Circuits 3(3), 1968, and A. S. Sedra and K. C. Smith, Microelectronic Circuits, the NMOS inverter with a resistive load; with beta = KP W/L = 2e-3 A/V^2, Vov = Vin - VTO and no channel-length modulation, cut-off for Vov <= 0: no drain current, so the output is the supply, 5 V

cases.title: Inverting amplifier with 1 kohm and 2 kohm and an op-amp of gain 1e6, input 1 V: output
cases.tolerance_note: chosen here: the ideal gain is -R2/R1; the finite open-loop gain 1e6 of the model lowers it by the factor 1 + (1 + R2/R1)/A = 1 + 3e-6, which is 6e-6 V at 2 V, so 2e-5 V is wider than that error
cases.source: A. S. Sedra and K. C. Smith, Microelectronic Circuits, the inverting configuration of an ideal op-amp: Vout/Vin = -R2/R1

cases.title: Voltage-controlled switch (on 100 ohm) closed by a 5 V control into a 900 ohm load on 5 V: load voltage
cases.tolerance_note: chosen here: the control is 2.5 V above the threshold with a transition half width of 0.1 V, so the conductance is within 1e-21 of its on value and the divider is exact up to rounding
cases.source: voltage divider of the on resistance and the load (J. W. Nilsson and S. A. Riedel, Electric Circuits): Vout = 5 x 900/(900 + 100)

cases.title: Voltage-controlled switch (off 1e9 ohm) opened by a 0 V control into a 900 ohm load on 5 V: load voltage
cases.tolerance_note: chosen here: the control is 2.5 V below the threshold, so the conductance is within 1e-21 of its off value and the divider is exact up to rounding
cases.source: voltage divider of the off resistance and the load (J. W. Nilsson and S. A. Riedel, Electric Circuits): Vout = 5 x 900/(900 + 1e9)
